result.summary: This PR adds an -ipcconnect option to bitcoin-gui so the GUI can attach to an already-running bitcoin-node process over IPC instead of always spawning its own node subprocess, letting the GUI be started and stopped independently. It is the last commit in a long stack (based on #29409, #10102, #19460) and the visible diff also carries all of those unmerged base commits: capnp wrappers for Chain/Wallet/Node/Handler interfaces, a libmultiprocess subtree bump, and a fix making btcsignals destroy disconnected callbacks eagerly. The description states default -ipcconnect=auto tries an existing node socket first and falls back to spawning a new node, with -noipcconnect, -ipcconnect (require), and -ipcconnect=unix:<path> variants.
result.problem: Currently the GUI can only run by spawning and owning its own node process, so users cannot run a long-lived headless node and attach/detach a GUI to it independently, something operators of the experimental multiprocess build want as part of the process-separation project (tracked in #28722).

open_concerns: Sjors reported (2023-02, 2023-05) that stopping the node after the GUI disconnects causes an uncaught ipc::Exception and a crash (SIGABRT); author reproduced and filed libmultiprocess issue #169 but no fix has landed yet.
Sjors also found GUI asserts (sendcoinsdialog.cpp) when using an external signer over the connected setup; not yet investigated.
jimhashhq (2025-03) reported bitcoin-node crashes if bitcoin-gui connects without matching -disablewallet settings; acknowledged by author as a real bug to fix.
laanwj raised a minor question about comma-separated option help text; resolved by dropping the nonstandard formatting.
resolved_concerns: Naming of the -ipcconnect option itself was accepted without objection (laanwj: 'ipcconnect SGTM as option name').

categories.name: utils
categories.evidence: btcsignals.h/.cpp changes make disconnect() destroy callback state eagerly instead of leaving it alive until a later connect() call, with new characterization and regression tests in test/btcsignals_tests.cpp; also touches util/result.h default-construction behavior.
categories.rationale: Commit message: 'a disconnected callback and any state it owned could stay alive indefinitely... That made destruction timing unpredictable for callbacks that own resources whose release has side effects,' concretely causing the multiprocess GUI test to hang. This is a real correctness fix to shared node-wide infrastructure (btcsignals is used across init/shutdown), not merely IPC-scoped, but it was found and motivated entirely by this stack's needs and has no independent bug report driving it.

categories.rationale: These are mechanical call-site/API adjustments required by the IPC serialization layer, not substantive wallet behavior changes, matching the exclusion for mechanical edits that follow from a change elsewhere.

uncertainties: The provided diff spans the entire unmerged stack (#29409, #10102, #19460, plus this PR's own commit), so it is unclear how much of the reviewed content is properly attributable to this specific PR versus its bases; category assessments above err toward crediting the whole visible diff since that is what a reviewer opening this PR would see.
No maintainer has weighed in on the specific -ipcconnect design since 2022; whether laanwj's 2020 concept ACK still reflects current maintainer sentiment after 5+ years and many rebases is unclear.
It is unclear whether the reported crash bugs (shutdown abort, external-signer assert) have since been fixed in later force-pushes; the discussion log does not show a resolution.
result.card: This PR adds an -ipcconnect option to bitcoin-gui so it can attach to an already-running bitcoin-node process instead of always spawning its own, letting the GUI start and stop independently of the node as part of the multiprocess process-separation project (#28722). It sits atop a long stack (#29409, #10102, #19460) and its visible diff also carries those unmerged base commits, including capnp interface wrappers and a real btcsignals fix that makes disconnected callbacks destroy eagerly. Two members gave concept ACK on the option itself, but live testing by Sjors turned up real unresolved crash bugs (node aborts on GUI shutdown, GUI assert with external signer) that the author has tracked but not yet fixed. The PR has been open since 2020, is still draft, and has been rebased dozens of times as the underlying stack evolved; it should be reviewed alongside its base PRs. Its core importance is as the concrete enabling step for GUI/node process separation, tempered by the fact that it only affects the experimental multiprocess build and has known reliability rough edges.
